transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I, uh... I came in because... I just can't shake this thought. I've been an electrician for years, you know? And... if all that experience couldn't keep my own brother safe, then... I don't know. I just feel like I'm a danger to anybody who works with me. Or even... anyone who lives under my roof.
Do you find yourself repeatedly thinking about this idea that you're a danger to others, even when you try to focus on something else?

Yeah. It's... it's just always there. I try to work, I try to just watch TV or something, but... yeah. It just keeps coming back. I just can't shake it. Like I said, if all those years doing this couldn't keep him safe... then I'm just a danger. To the guys at work, to... to everyone. It just doesn't stop.
Do you feel like you have to do anything specific to try to make these thoughts go away or to prevent anything bad from happening?
No... not really. I don't... do anything like that. I just... try to keep my head down, I guess. There's not really anything I can do to fix it anyway.
Do you ever feel like you need to repeat certain actions or behaviors to try to make these thoughts go away?
No. Like I just said, I don't really do anything. Just... sit with it, I guess.
Do you feel anxious when things are not done a certain way or in a specific order?
No. I don't really care about that kind of stuff. I just... no.
Do you feel an overwhelming urge to think of something specific to counteract these thoughts about being a danger to others?
No. I don't... I don't do that. Like I said, I don't really try to counteract them or anything. They're just... they're just there.
Are these thoughts about being a danger to others intrusive, meaning they come into your mind without you wanting them to?

Yeah. They just... happen. I'll be in the middle of wiring a panel, or... or I'll hear my nephew shut the garage door, and suddenly I'm just... right back there. Smelling smoke. Seeing my brother. It's like the job site just drops out from under me. I don't ask for it to happen. It just does.
Do you feel like you have to think of something specific to make these thoughts about being a danger to others less upsetting?
No. Like I just said, I don't... I don't do that. There's no specific thought or anything that makes it less upsetting. I just... I just have to wait for it to pass.
Do you think these thoughts about being a danger to others are true, or do they seem irrational to you?

I... I think they're true. 

I mean... I've been doing this for a long time. And if all my years as an electrician couldn't keep my own brother safe... then yeah. I can't shake it. I just... I feel like I'm a danger to anybody who works with me, or... or lives under my roof. 

That's... that's why I came in.
Do you feel like you have to think or do something to neutralize or undo the thoughts that you're a danger to others?
No. I... I don't do anything like that. I just told you, I... I just wait for it to pass.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a danger to others are a part of you, or do they feel like they're coming from outside of yourself?
I don't... I don't really know what you mean by that. They're just... my thoughts. They're in my head. I don't hear voices or anything, if that's what you're asking. It's just me.
Do you ever feel the need to check on people or things to make sure they are safe?
No, I... I don't really do that. I just... I just keep to myself, mostly.
Do these thoughts about being a danger to others feel like they are a part of who you are, or do they feel foreign to you?
I... didn't you just ask me that? I don't really know what you mean by foreign. Like I said, they're just... they're just my thoughts. It's just me.
Do you feel like you need to make amends or take specific actions to make up for what happened to your brother?
I don't... no. I mean, there's nothing I can really do. He's gone. I just try not to think about it, mostly.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a danger to others are in line with your own beliefs and values?
I don't... I don't really know how to answer that. Values? I don't think about it like that. I just... I'm not trying to hurt anybody, if that's what you mean. They're just things in my head.
Do you feel guilty about what happened to your brother?

...Yeah. I guess. It's just... this heavy feeling. Like a mix of guilt and... anger, maybe. Just sitting in my chest all day. It's hard when... when I look at my nephew. Just... knowing he lost his dad, and... he got stuck with me instead.
How long have you been experiencing these thoughts about being a danger to others?
...About four months, I guess. Since... since the fire in the garage. And when my nephew moved in.
Have these thoughts about being a danger to others made it harder for you to do your job or take care of things at home?

Yeah... I guess. Work's been... slipping, lately. It's gotten to the point where the apprentices won't even pair up with me anymore. And... I actually got pulled off a solar job recently. There was a... a confrontation. They told me I wasn't safe to have on site. So... yeah. I guess it is.
Do you feel like you need to do something specific to try to make up for the guilt you feel about what happened to your brother?
...No. Not really. I just... I just try to get through the day. There's nothing I can do to fix it anyway.
